subject.title: Video-generation providers fetch the result URL with no SSRF guard (byteplus, minimax, xai, runway, vydra)

question: Should this SSRF report stay in the public provider-hardening flow, or should maintainers move it into private OpenClaw security handling before implementation?
rationale: The source path is concrete and security-sensitive, but disclosure and handling for compromised-provider or malicious custom-endpoint SSRF is a maintainer security-boundary choice.

options.title: Fix Publicly As Provider Hardening
options.body: Keep this issue open publicly and land a focused guarded-download fix with default-deny SSRF regression tests across the affected providers.

options.title: Move To Private Security Handling
options.body: Transfer implementation and discussion into the security process if maintainers judge the threat model to require private coordination.

options.title: Coordinate Partial Provider PRs
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical tracker while existing provider-specific PRs are corrected or replaced until all five affected paths are covered.

recommendation.title: Fix Publicly As Provider Hardening
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open publicly and land a focused guarded-download fix with default-deny SSRF regression tests across the affected providers.

likelyOwner.reason: The affected video provider files most consistently trace to Peter Steinberger's provider-introduction commits, and the choice is a security-boundary/product-maintenance decision.
